<reason>B won by keeping the motion as a default-versus-reason-to-look rule and making that clash easier to decide. B showed ordinary care (curfews, check-ins, looking when something is off) is not neglect, answered how parents can see a missed curfew or secrecy without a live dashboard, and turned A’s hardest cases against A’s tool. A’s irreversible-harm weighing stayed vivid but was undercut once B split location-after-a-failed-check-in from always-on reading of friend chats, and once A conceded you cannot sort intimacy from infiltration without looking.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2: a missed curfew is an empty house, not GPS history; and if grooming is designed to look normal, default scrolling of ordinary chats fails the same cases used to justify standing inspection of intimacy.</best_rebuttal>
